Official cumulative QPI versus major GPA

helpIntro: Georgetown undergraduate GPA is the cumulative Quality Point Index (QPI): multiply each quality grade by course credits, total the quality points, and divide by attempted quality-grade credits.
helpNote: For main-campus undergraduate QPI only. S/U and most external grades are excluded. Georgetown truncates the official QPI to three decimals without rounding; this planning calculator displays three decimals using normal rounding. Repeat Impact is disabled because Georgetown repeat treatment depends on the original result.
helpExample: A 3-credit A earns 12.00 quality points and a 4-credit B+ earns 13.32. Together, 25.32 ÷ 7 = 3.617142…, so Georgetown’s official QPI is 3.617.

gradeExplanations.F: F = 0.00; attempted credits still count in the QPI denominator.
gradeExplanations.S: Satisfactory pass/fail grade; earns credit but does not affect QPI.
gradeExplanations.U: Unsatisfactory pass/fail grade; no credit and does not affect QPI.
gradeExplanations.N: Provisional undergraduate grade; wait for the final grade before calculating.
gradeExplanations.AU: Audit carries no quality points and is excluded from QPI.

specialTypes.name: Georgetown undergraduate course
specialTypes.note: Use the undergraduate grade table for Georgetown main-campus undergraduate coursework, including Georgetown-administered work that posts to the cumulative QPI.

specialTypes.name: External transfer, most study abroad, or consortium credit
specialTypes.note: Credits may apply to the degree, but external grades generally do not enter the cumulative QPI.

specialTypes.name: Law, graduate, or another grading system
specialTypes.note: Do not apply the undergraduate 4.0/QPI map to a different Georgetown academic record.

repeatPolicy.note: Repeat Impact is disabled. If you repeat a failed course and pass, enter both attempts as separate completed rows; consult your dean for any other repeat situation.
